Suppose that the vector [MATH: \mathbf{a}] has magnitude [MATH: 7,] the vector [MATH: \mathbf{b}] has magnitude [MATH: 6,] and the angle between the vectors is [MATH: \theta=45^\circ.] Then the magnitude of the cross product [MATH: \mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}] is

Content:
[MATH: |a × b||=|a||b|\sin θ; = 7 ⋅ 6 ⋅ \sin 45^{∘}; = 7 ⋅ 6 ⋅ (sqrt(2))/(2); = 21sqrt(2).]

Content:

So the magnitude of the cross product represents the area of the parallelogram spanned by the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b},] as shown in the picture below.

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of the triangle is [MATH: A_{\triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{\sqrt{554}}{2}.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we find the vectors [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: AB^(→)|= b − a; = (− 2i + k) − (i − 2k); = − 3i + 3k; = ⟨ − 3, 0, 3⟩; AC^(→)|= c − a; = (i + j − k) − (i − 2k); = j + k; = ⟨0, 1, 1⟩]

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

[MATH: AB^(→) × AC^(→)|=|i|j|k; − 3|0|3; 0|1|1|; =|0|3; 1|1|i −|− 3|3; 0|1|j +|− 3|0; 0|1|k; = (0 ⋅ 1 − 3 ⋅ 1)i − (− 3 ⋅ 1 − 3 ⋅ 0)j + (− 3 ⋅ 1 − 0 ⋅ 0)k; = − 3i + 3j − 3k; = ⟨ − 3, 3, − 3⟩.]

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}] is [MATH: A|=|AB^(→) × AC^(→)|; = sqrt((− 3)^{2} + 3^{2} + (− 3)^{2}); = 3sqrt(3).]

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of [MATH: \bigtriangleup\!ABC] is

[MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.]

sections.normalized_html:
Note that the length of the altitude [MATH: CH] can be related to the area of [MATH: \bigtriangleup\!ABC] as follows:

[MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB]

So, to find [MATH: CH,] we first find [MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup}.] To start, we find the vectors [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: AB^(→)|= b − a; = (i + j + 2k) − (− i + j); = 2i + 2k; = ⟨2, 0, 2⟩; AC^(→)|= c − a; = (i − j + k) − (− i + j); = 2i − 2j + k; = ⟨2, − 2, 1⟩]

Now, we have

[MATH: AB^(→) × AC^(→)|=|i|j|k; 2|0|2; 2|− 2|1|; =|0|2; − 2|1|i −|2|2; 2|1|j +|2|0; 2|− 2|k; = (0 ⋅ 1 − 2 ⋅ (− 2))i − (2 ⋅ 1 − 2 ⋅ 2)j + (2 ⋅ (− 2) − 0 ⋅ 2)k; = 4i + 2j − 4k; = ⟨4, 2, − 4⟩.]

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}] is

[MATH: A|=|AB^(→) × AC^(→)|; = sqrt(4^{2} + 2^{2} + (− 4)^{2}); = sqrt(36); = 6.]

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of [MATH: \bigtriangleup\!ABC] is

[MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 6 = 3.]

Let's also compute [MATH: AB] since it appears in the formula:

[MATH: AB|=|AB^(→)|; = sqrt(2^{2} + 0^{2} + 2^{2}); = sqrt(8); = 2sqrt(2)]

Finally, using the formula [MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB,] we get

[MATH: A_{△}|= (1)/(2)CH ⋅ AB; 3|= (1)/(2)CH ⋅ 2sqrt(2); 3|= CH ⋅ sqrt(2); CH|= (3)/(sqrt(2)); CH|= (3sqrt(2))/(2).]

Item 2 — Example: Calculating the Area of the Triangle Spanned by Two Vectors

Example Prompt:
Calculate the area of the triangle spanned by [MATH: \mathbf{a}=\langle 4,0,-3 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}=\langle 5,-1,2 \rangle.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Using the formula, we have

[MATH: a × b|=|i|j|k; 4|0|− 3; 5|− 1|2|; =|0|− 3; − 1|2|i −|4|− 3; 5|2|j +|4|0; 5|− 1|k; = (0 ⋅ 2 − (− 3) ⋅ (− 1))i − (4 ⋅ 2 − (− 3) ⋅ 5)j + (4 ⋅ (− 1) − 0 ⋅ 5)k; = − 3i − 23j − 4k; = ⟨ − 3, − 23, − 4⟩.]

Therefore, the area of the corresponding parallelogram is
[MATH: A|=|a × b|; = sqrt((− 3)^{2} + (− 23)^{2} + (− 4)^{2}); = sqrt(554).]

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of the triangle is
[MATH: A_{\triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{\sqrt{554}}{2}.]

Item 5 — Example: Calculating the Area of a Triangle Given Its Vertices

Example Prompt:

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we find the vectors [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: AB^(→)|= b − a; = (− 2i + k) − (i − 2k); = − 3i + 3k; = ⟨ − 3, 0, 3⟩; AC^(→)|= c − a; = (i + j − k) − (i − 2k); = j + k; = ⟨0, 1, 1⟩]

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

[MATH: AB^(→) × AC^(→)|=|i|j|k; − 3|0|3; 0|1|1|; =|0|3; 1|1|i −|− 3|3; 0|1|j +|− 3|0; 0|1|k; = (0 ⋅ 1 − 3 ⋅ 1)i − (− 3 ⋅ 1 − 3 ⋅ 0)j + (− 3 ⋅ 1 − 0 ⋅ 0)k; = − 3i + 3j − 3k; = ⟨ − 3, 3, − 3⟩.]

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}] is
[MATH: A|=|AB^(→) × AC^(→)|; = sqrt((− 3)^{2} + 3^{2} + (− 3)^{2}); = 3sqrt(3).]

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of [MATH: \bigtriangleup\!ABC] is

Item 8 — Example: Calculating the Altitude of a Triangle Given Its Vertices

Example Prompt:
Calculate the length of the altitude [MATH: CH] of the [MATH: \bigtriangleup\!ABC] if [MATH: A(-1,1,0),] [MATH: B(1,1,2),] [MATH: C(1,-1,1).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Note that the length of the altitude [MATH: CH] can be related to the area of [MATH: \bigtriangleup\!ABC] as follows:

[MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB]

So, to find [MATH: CH,] we first find [MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup}.] To start, we find the vectors [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: AB^(→)|= b − a; = (i + j + 2k) − (− i + j); = 2i + 2k; = ⟨2, 0, 2⟩; AC^(→)|= c − a; = (i − j + k) − (− i + j); = 2i − 2j + k; = ⟨2, − 2, 1⟩]

Now, we have

[MATH: AB^(→) × AC^(→)|=|i|j|k; 2|0|2; 2|− 2|1|; =|0|2; − 2|1|i −|2|2; 2|1|j +|2|0; 2|− 2|k; = (0 ⋅ 1 − 2 ⋅ (− 2))i − (2 ⋅ 1 − 2 ⋅ 2)j + (2 ⋅ (− 2) − 0 ⋅ 2)k; = 4i + 2j − 4k; = ⟨4, 2, − 4⟩.]

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by [MATH: \overrightarrow{AB}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}] is

[MATH: A|=|AB^(→) × AC^(→)|; = sqrt(4^{2} + 2^{2} + (− 4)^{2}); = sqrt(36); = 6.]

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of [MATH: \bigtriangleup\!ABC] is

[MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 6 = 3.]

Let's also compute [MATH: AB] since it appears in the formula:

[MATH: AB|=|AB^(→)|; = sqrt(2^{2} + 0^{2} + 2^{2}); = sqrt(8); = 2sqrt(2)]

Finally, using the formula [MATH: A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB,] we get

[MATH: A_{△}|= (1)/(2)CH ⋅ AB; 3|= (1)/(2)CH ⋅ 2sqrt(2); 3|= CH ⋅ sqrt(2); CH|= (3)/(sqrt(2)); CH|= (3sqrt(2))/(2).]
